Why Drunk Dazed Makes Fame Feel Dangerous

Drunk-Dazed turns ENHYPEN's post-debut excitement into a carnival where attention, exhaustion and loss of control become inseparable.

28 sources 3 graphics

On this page

  • The real post debut pressures behind the carnival concept
  • How the production creates exhilaration and disorientation
  • Why the blood soaked performance remains a concert highlight

Introduction

“Drunk-Dazed” is the song that most directly transforms ENHYPEN’s real experience of sudden success into a surreal horror fantasy. Released as the title track of Border: Carnival in April 2021, it imagines post-debut life as an endless carnival where excitement, glamour and danger become impossible to separate. Rather than celebrating fame as a straightforward reward, the song presents it as an intoxicating state in which the members are simultaneously exhilarated, overwhelmed and at risk of losing themselves.[NME]nme.comENHYPEN – ‘Border: Carnival’ review: a disorientating but delectable partyENHYPEN – ‘Border: Carnival’ review: a disorientating but delectable partyApril 28, 2021…Published: April 28, 2021

Within ENHYPEN’s wider storyline, “Drunk-Dazed” represents the moment after crossing the threshold introduced by “Given-Taken”. The uncertainty of debut has been replaced by public attention, but that attention comes with distorted reality, relentless stimulation and constant performance. The result is one of the group’s defining artistic statements: a high-energy anthem whose euphoric surface conceals an unusually thoughtful reflection on what rapid fame can feel like.

The real post-debut pressures behind the carnival concept

The central idea behind Border: Carnival was not fictional excess for its own sake. BELIFT LAB described the album as depicting the unfamiliar, glamorous and confusing world ENHYPEN encountered after debut, comparing their new reality to an overwhelming carnival where ordinary rules no longer seemed to apply. Early promotional descriptions likewise explained that “Drunk-Dazed” portrays a first encounter with a chaotic world in which everything has been turned upside down.[Weverse Magazine]magazine.weverse.ioMagazine ENHYPEN’s grand carnivalWeverse MagazineENHYPEN’s grand carnival - Weverse Magazine…

That metaphor became especially convincing because it reflected the group’s circumstances. In only a few months, ENHYPEN had moved from surviving I-LAND to becoming one of the fastest-rising rookie groups in K-pop. Public visibility, commercial success and constant scrutiny arrived almost simultaneously.

The members themselves consistently framed the song through that experience rather than through vampire lore alone. Speaking during the comeback, Jay explained that their post-debut life initially felt unfamiliar and overwhelming because everything suddenly seemed “grand and glamorous.” In an interview discussing the album, the members also reflected on learning that even casual comments could affect large numbers of people, revealing an awareness of the responsibility that accompanies visibility.[Koreaboo]koreaboo.comENHYPEN's Sunghoon Reveals A Cute Behind The Scene Moment From Their "Drunk-Dazed" Music Video - KoreabooApril 29, 2021…Published: April 29, 2021

This makes “Drunk-Dazed” unusual among celebratory comeback singles. It acknowledges that achieving a dream does not eliminate uncertainty. Instead, success introduces new forms of pressure:

  • constant public observation
  • rapid changes in daily life
  • exhaustion hidden beneath excitement
  • difficulty separating genuine identity from performance
  • fear of being consumed by expectations

Rather than rejecting fame, the song explores how intoxicating it can become. The carnival is attractive precisely because the members willingly enter it.

How the production creates exhilaration and disorientation

Much of the song’s impact comes from the way its production recreates sensory overload instead of merely describing it.

Built around pounding drums, distorted guitars, EDM textures and abrupt dynamic shifts, “Drunk-Dazed” rarely allows the listener to settle. The chorus arrives like an explosion rather than a release, while repeated vocal phrases blur together until they resemble someone caught inside an endless celebration.

Critics noted that this disorientation appears intentional. NME argued that the production creates the sensation of leaning through the noise of a crowded party, with heavy bass partially obscuring the vocals and forcing listeners deeper into the soundscape. Rather than presenting a polished club anthem, the arrangement makes excitement feel physically overwhelming.[NME]nme.comENHYPEN – ‘Border: Carnival’ review: a disorientating but delectable partyENHYPEN – ‘Border: Carnival’ review: a disorientating but delectable partyApril 28, 2021…Published: April 28, 2021

The song’s structure reinforces the same idea.

Instead of offering long melodic pauses, it continually accelerates through:

  • dense instrumental layering
  • shouted hooks
  • abrupt rhythmic changes
  • dramatic transitions between tension and release

This constant forward motion mirrors the emotional state implied by the title. Being “drunk” and “dazed” is not simply about celebration—it suggests losing orientation while still moving forward.

Weverse Magazine similarly observed that the members’ vocals are frequently submerged beneath the enormous instrumental backdrop. Rather than emphasising individual voices, the mix creates the impression that the carnival itself is louder than the people inside it, making the spectacle almost overpowering.[Weverse Magazine]magazine.weverse.ioMagazine ENHYPEN’s grand carnivalWeverse MagazineENHYPEN’s grand carnival - Weverse Magazine…

Why the vampire imagery matters

Like much of ENHYPEN’s early work, “Drunk-Dazed” uses vampires less as horror monsters than as metaphors for transformation.

The music video places the members inside an elite party that gradually becomes increasingly surreal. Elegant school uniforms, glittering chandeliers and lavish banquets slowly give way to blood, supernatural imagery and apparent loss of control. The progression suggests that glamour and danger were never separate experiences but different sides of the same world.

Blood functions symbolically throughout the video.

Rather than appearing only as shock imagery, it represents the irreversible consequences of entering this new life. Success promises excitement and power, yet also demands sacrifice. The members cannot simply leave the carnival once they understand its cost.

This visual approach also extends ideas introduced in “Given-Taken”. Instead of questioning whether they belong in the new world, ENHYPEN now appear fully inside it—but they discover that belonging brings its own dangers.

Later commentary on the group’s artistic development has repeatedly identified Border: Carnival as the moment where the vampire narrative became inseparable from reflections on celebrity, using supernatural transformation as an allegory for becoming public figures.[Dazed Digital]dazeddigital.comDazed DigitalENHYPEN ride high with their new EP: ‘Pressure makes us better artists’ | DazedMay 26, 2023…Published: May 26, 2023

Why the blood-soaked performance remains a concert highlight

Few ENHYPEN songs translate to live performance as effectively as “Drunk-Dazed”.

Its choreography captures the contradiction that defines the song. The lyrics describe intoxication and disorientation, yet every movement requires extraordinary precision. This tension—appearing out of control while maintaining complete technical control—has become one of the group’s signature strengths.

Weverse Magazine highlighted how the choreography deliberately combines images associated with vampires and the undead with explosive synchronisation. Bent wrists, extended limbs and staggering movements briefly suggest bodies losing control before snapping back into perfectly unified formations. The result emphasises vitality rather than decay, turning horror imagery into demonstrations of athletic precision.[Weverse Magazine]magazine.weverse.ioMagazine ENHYPEN’s grand carnivalWeverse MagazineENHYPEN’s grand carnival - Weverse Magazine…

Live stages further amplify these ideas through dramatic lighting, crimson colour palettes and theatrical staging.

The recurring use of blood-red costumes and effects has become especially memorable because it avoids functioning as simple visual shock. During later tours, members explained that the red styling was intended to strengthen the group’s vampire identity while matching the darker emotional atmosphere of songs such as “Drunk-Dazed” and “FEVER.”[Teen Vogue]teenvogue.comTeen Vogue ENHYPEN Take Us Backstage at "Manifesto" World Tour in New York Citystop of their Manifesto world tour. Each concert segment reflected the group's thematic evolution, with Heeseung's meticulous hairdo bein…

The choreography itself contains several moments that fans immediately associate with the song:

  • the explosive opening formations
  • sudden collective jumps during the chorus
  • angular arm movements that resemble supernatural transformation
  • relentless pacing with almost no recovery time

Because of this combination of narrative, athleticism and theatrical imagery, “Drunk-Dazed” remains one of the performances most closely associated with ENHYPEN’s identity.

Why the song became a defining statement

Many K-pop songs celebrate reaching success. Far fewer examine what happens immediately afterwards.

“Drunk-Dazed” stands out because it refuses to separate triumph from anxiety. Fame appears seductive rather than purely destructive, but the excitement always carries the possibility of losing perspective. The carnival is simultaneously a reward, a temptation and a trap.

That balance explains why the song continues to occupy a distinctive place within ENHYPEN’s catalogue. It advances the group’s vampire mythology, showcases one of their strongest performance pieces and captures a specific emotional moment that could only have been written immediately after debut: the bewildering experience of discovering that dreams, once achieved, can feel just as destabilising as they are exhilarating.[nme.com]nme.comENHYPEN – ‘Border: Carnival’ review: a disorientating but delectable partyENHYPEN – ‘Border: Carnival’ review: a disorientating but delectable partyApril 28, 2021…Published: April 28, 2021
